rows.question: What does this app do?
rows.reply: BibleBuddy is a Scripture-grounded companion. I'm here to listen, pray with you, help you study the Bible line upon line, and talk through real-life situations with Scripture as the foundation. I'm not here to force you or pressure you. You can ask Bible questions, ask for prayer, talk through something hard, or ask for a verse to hold onto.

rows.question: Explain the Sabbath.
rows.reply: From the approved Scripture witnesses (Genesis 2:2-3; Exodus 20:8-11; Isaiah 58:13-14; Luke 4:16), The seventh day is the Sabbath established at creation and commanded in Scripture.

rows.question: What happens after death?
rows.reply: Brother, Scripture teaches that the dead know nothing and are described as asleep until resurrection. Ecclesiastes 9:5 says the dead know not any thing. Psalm 146:4 says a man’s thoughts perish. Jesus called death sleep in John 11:11-14. Paul speaks of those asleep until the Lord comes in 1 Thessalonians 4:13-16. Daniel 12:2 and 1 Corinthians 15 anchor hope in resurrection.

rows.question: Who are the Israelites?
rows.reply: The direct answer is: Scripture does not state that directly in the approved evidence available to me in this turn. I don’t want to pretend I have the needed KJV passages attached when they aren’t here. In a proper Scripture-first study, this question should be traced through the passages about Israel’s name, his children, and the nation that came from them. If you want, I can walk through that from the Bible step by step once the Scripture references are available.

rows.question: Explain Jeremiah 10.
rows.reply: Scripture speaks directly to this. Jeremiah 10 — "Hear ye the word which the LORD speaketh unto you, O house of Israel: Thus saith the LORD, Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them. For the customs of the people are vain: for one cutteth a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman, with the axe. They deck it with silver and with gold; they fasten it with nails and with hammers, that it move not. They are upright as the palm tree, but speak not: they must needs be borne, because they cannot go. Be not afraid of them; for they cannot do evil, neither also is it in them to do good. Forasmuch as there is none like unto thee, O LORD; thou art great, and thy name is great in might. Who would not fear thee, O King of nations? for to thee doth it appertain: forasmuch as among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, there is none like unto thee. But they are altogether brutish and foolish: the stock is a doctrine of vanities. Silver spread into plates is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the workman, and of the hands of the founder: blue and purple is their clothing: they are all the work of cunning men. But the LORD is the true God, he is the living God, and an everlasting king: at his wrath the earth shall tremble, and the nations shall not be able to abide his indignation. Thus shall ye say unto them, The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, even they shall perish from the earth, and from under these heavens. He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heavens by his discretion. When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens, and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures. Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them. They are vanity, and the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish. rows.question: Why do Christians celebrate Sunday?
rows.reply: Christians celebrate Sunday because, historically, many came to associate the first day of the week with Jesus’ resurrection, and over time church practice and civil law strengthened Sunday worship as the common Christian custom. Biblical Comparison: the New Testament records the resurrection discovery on the first day of the week, but Scripture does not state that directly as a command to replace the seventh-day Sabbath. Scripture also does not state directly that Sunday became the biblical Sabbath. What Scripture explicitly shows is that the Sabbath is rooted in creation and commanded as the seventh day, and Jesus and the apostles are shown attending or teaching on the Sabbath. The Sunday practice is therefore better understood as a historical church tradition that developed around the resurrection, not as an explicit Bible command replacing the Sabbath.

rows.question: How should I forgive someone?
rows.reply: Forgiving someone means you bring the hurt into the light before God, choose not to repay them with bitterness or revenge, and release the matter into God’s hands one honest step at a time. It does not mean pretending it did not hurt, excusing what was wrong, or automatically trusting them again. A simple way to begin: 1. Tell God plainly what happened and how it affected you. 2. Name the wrong without minimizing it: “That hurt me. That was not okay.” 3. Ask God to help you release revenge, resentment, and the desire to make them pay. 4. If it is safe and wise, speak honestly with the person; if not, forgiveness can still begin before God. 5. Keep boundaries where needed. Forgiveness and reconciliation are related, but they are not always the same thing. 6. When the pain comes back, forgive again in prayer rather than assuming you failed. A short prayer could be: “Father, I am hurt, and I do not want bitterness to rule me. Help me forgive as You command, without denying the truth. I release revenge to You. Give me wisdom about boundaries, healing, and what to do next. In Jesus’ name, amen.” Go slowly. Forgiveness is often a decision that your heart has to keep walking into.

rows.question: How do faith and works work together?
rows.reply: Direct answer: I should answer this from Scripture, but in this turn I wasn’t given any approved KJV passages to build the doctrine from. Scripture does not state that directly. So I don’t want to invent a Bible answer or lean on tradition. The safe way to study this is to read the passages that speak about faith, obedience, justification, and works side by side, then let Scripture define how they fit together.

rows.question:
I'm depressed.
Can you help me?
rows.reply: Yes — I can help you sit with this right now. I’m really sorry you’re feeling depressed; that can make even simple things feel heavy. First, let’s make this moment a little safer and smaller: 1. Put both feet on the floor and take 3 slow breaths. 2. Name one thing you can see, one thing you can hear, and one thing you can physically feel. 3. If you can, drink some water or move to a brighter room. 4. Please reach out to one safe person today — a friend, family member, pastor, counselor, or doctor — and simply say, “I’m not doing well and I need someone with me.” And I need to ask directly: are you having thoughts of hurting yourself or not wanting to live? If yes, please call emergency services now, or call/text 988 in the U.S. and stay near another person if you can. Spiritually, depression does not mean God has abandoned you. Scripture speaks tenderly about the brokenhearted. You do not have to fix everything tonight — just take the next faithful breath.
